Hi Samira — thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we keep momentum: 

What we covered (2 high-level items):
- Core use case: automated payment reconciliation assistant (high-sensitivity numeracy + multi-turn context across statements).
- Success criteria: micro-F1 on entity extraction > 92% (internal baseline), generation precision for amounts/ledgers within 1% error budget, and no human-detectable hallucinations in 95% of sampled transcripts.

Redwood recommended model paths (based on your latency & cost preferences):
- Open candidate (cost-optimized): Luminous-Open-32q (8-bit quantized) — expected parity for NLU intents, lower hallucination control, best cost per token.
- Proprietary baseline (your current vendor): ProprietaryPay-v2 (what you showed us) — stronger arithmetic consistency in long sequences.
- Redwood hybrid suggestion: run Luminous-Open-32q + a small guarded reranker (Redwood lightweight reranker) to reduce hallucinations and bring recall/precision in line with your baseline.

Suggested trial scope (2-week pilot):
1) Ingest 10k anonymized reconciliation transcripts (you provide sample set).
2) Run three evaluation buckets: open-model-only, baseline-only (your exported runs), and open+reranker.
3) Metrics: entity micro-F1, amount error (%), hallucination incidence (human-reviewed sample), avg latency p95.

Acceptance thresholds we discussed (draft):
- Entity micro-F1 >= 0.90 for trial to be considered successful.
- Amount error <= 1.5% mean absolute percentage error.
- Hallucination rate <= 5% on human sample of 200 dialogs.
- p95 latency <= 850ms for single-request path.

Action items / next steps: 
- Samira: confirm dataset share (S3 link or Drive) and point of contact for procurement + security.
- Procurement: we may need an NDA + DPA; Mateo to introduce the right Redwood contacts after your confirmation.
- Redwood: we will prepare an evaluation bundle (prompt sets, benchmark harness, dashboard) and a mutual action plan.

Attachments included in this email: aureum_trial_prompt_bundle_v1.json (sample prompts + guidance), redwood-benchmark-report-llm-open-vs-baseline.pdf (representative benchmarks we ran on similar workloads), mutual-action-plan-aureum-2026.xlsx (high-level timeline + owners).

If that aligns, I'll queue the trial and propose Wed 8/19 11am PT for a short kickoff with engineering.

Best,
Mateo Alvarez
Senior Solutions Associate
Redwood Inference

Mateo / Samira — quick internal note on the three items Samira raised: 

1) Hallucination labeling template:
- We'll provide a 1-page labeling guide: definition, positive/negative examples, and edge cases (partial numbers, inferred payee names). I'll attach after this email. For consistency, we recommend two annotators per sample with majority vote; disagreements flagged for SME review.

2) Reranker latency model:
- Implementation options:
  a) Inline rerank (single round): candidates generated, then reranker selects top — p95 could increase by ~40–120ms depending on batch sizing.
  b) Async post-process: generate, return best-effort to user, then update final reconciliation in the background (no impact on p95 user path).

Given your p95 constraint, option (b) may be a safer default for the pilot unless you want very tight final accuracy on the first-touch. We'll instrument both and report.

3) Cost estimate (very rough for procurement):
- Open-only (Luminous-Open-32q): ~ $1,200 for processing 10k dialogs (token mix estimate included in the deck).
- Open + reranker (hybrid): ~ $1,800 (adds reranker token and compute).
- If you want reserved/dedicated capacity the unit economics will change — we can provide an alternate quote.

I'll follow up with the labeling guide and a small latency microbench report.

— Priyom
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks for looping me in — a couple practical points from the eval team to reduce risk of quality regressions during the pilot: 

- Evaluation bundles: please include both prompt-locked and prompt-variation sets. Prompt-locked lets us compare apples-to-apples with your exported baseline; prompt-variation surfaces robustness.
- Regression alerting: we'll set up lightweight quality checks during the pilot — if entity micro-F1 drops by >3% vs baseline on consecutive daily checks, we trigger a manual review.
- Sampling plan: for the hallucination audit, sample 120 dialogs randomly + 80 high-risk dialogs (complex refunds, multi-party transfers). This lets us keep the human review budget manageable but targeted.
- Benchmarks: include at least one deterministic unit test (fixed input -> canonical output) to detect accidental nondeterminism introduced by model updates/temperature drift.

I'll attach a short checklist and the canonical unit test examples to the Hub Drive link. Once Samira confirms dataset share, we'll provision the evaluation sandbox and dashboards.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Staff ML Ops, Redwood Inference
